rationale: In `crates/trust-but-verify/src/structural.rs#mod[tests]/fn[rules_compile_for_every_grammar_and_report_invalid_input]`, assert for every bundled language that each `extensions()` entry is non-empty and does not start with '.'. A matching assertion could also check a known extension for each language, such as py, ts, tsx, css, md, toml and yaml/yml. — The `requirements.sdk.graph.search.StructuralRule` text says `extensions` lists filename extensions without leading dots. The tests check this only for rust, where `compile_once_and_search_supplied_source` asserts `extensions().contains(&"rs")`. For the other grammars they only assert `!rule.extensions().is_empty()`. Extensions come from per-language profile data. A profile that returned ".py", ".css" or ".md" would pass every reviewed test, because only non-emptiness is checked for those languages.

text: A `sources::StructuralRule` is a structural query compiled for repeated searches
of text supplied by the caller. `languages` lists the bundled grammar names
accepted by `compile`. Compilation reports an unknown language or an invalid
ast-grep rule core, even when there is no source to search. `extensions` lists
the language's filename extensions without leading dots and contains at least one entry.
`matches` searches the supplied UTF-8 text and returns distinct half-open byte
spans ordered by start, then end. Offsets refer to that input on each call.
`SourceProject::search_structure` uses the same matcher for project files.
